hints.title: Copy-Paste Character Multiplier Obstacle
hints.text: Starting with a single 'A', you can either Copy All or Paste the clipboard buffer. How can expressing the target n as a product of prime factors determine the minimum keystrokes needed?

hints.title: Prime Factor Decomposition Invariant
hints.text: Multiplying existing length by factor d requires 1 Copy All followed by d - 1 Paste operations (d total steps). The minimum steps to reach n equals the sum of its prime factors.

hints.title: Prime Factor Extraction Procedure
hints.text: Initialize step counter to 0 and factor d to 2. While n > 1, repeatedly divide n by d and add d to the step counter whenever d divides n. Increment d when d no longer divides n. Return total steps.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Extracts prime factors up to sqrt(N) in constant auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating buffer state trees takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant space factor extraction is optimal.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Connecting the Copy-Paste multiplier mechanics to prime factorization.
